item.title: Boston's Museum of Fine Arts announces layoffs
item.description: The museum notified employees of the layoffs in an internal email sent Tuesday. More than 30 museum positions will be affected.

item.title: How Minneapolis is standing up to ICE
item.description: In Minneapolis, grassroots groups have sprung into action against ICE. They’re protesting, running workshops on constitutional rights, and delivering groceries to people afraid of leaving their homes.

item.title: ICE operations in Maine are taking an emotional toll on the family and friends of those detained
item.description: ICE says its made than 200 arrests in Maine since expending operations in the state last week. And while the agency has said it's going after criminals, many of those detained are asylum seekers with no criminal records, according to their lawyers, family members and employers.

item.title: Starring Jodie Foster, 'A Private Life' is a character study in the guise of a thriller
item.description: The actress plays an American psychiatrist living in Paris. After one of her patients dies, she teams up with her ex-husband to solve what she believes is a murder. The role is one of Foster's "meatiest" in some time, film critic Sean Burns reviews.

item.title: Dance and sculpture defy gravity in ‘Noli Timere’
item.description: Sculptor Janet Echelman returns to Boston with a bold, innovative collaboration with choreographer Rebecca Lazier and composer Jorane. Noli Timere runs from Jan. 29 through Feb. 1 at the Emerson Cutler Majestic Theatre.

item.title: Our favorite local music from January
item.description: From a single inspired by larvae squirming in the dirt to a comically enlightening track about waiting on hold with an insurance company, our music critics share their favorite music from the month.

item.title: How a Cambridge developer's lawsuit could unravel an affordable housing policy
item.description: Patrick Barrett, with support from the Pioneer New England Legal Foundation, is challenging Cambridge’s requirement that 20% of all new developments include affordable units, a policy known as “inclusionary zoning.”

item.title: Inside the AI companies hiring in Boston
item.description: Anthropic, which makes the chatbot Claude; Lovable, which makes an AI tool that can create custom software; and xAI, Elon Musk's AI company which makes the chatbot Grok, are hiring in Boston.

item.title: Eating snow cones or snow cream can be a winter delight, if done safely
item.description: How safe is it to turn snow into a treat? Experts say eating a bit of snow is probably fine if you live someplace with generally clean air, but staying away from plowed snow is a sensible precaution.
